title: U$^3$CF: Unbiased, Unconfounding, and Unified Causal Framework for Multi-Target Domain Adaptation
claim: Prior methods train separate models per target domain and discard domain-specific features; ours uses one unified model guided by causal features.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line, bottom-to-top flow, SCM graph inset
description: The figure has two panels separated by a vertical dashed line. The left panel is labeled Previous Methods and the right panel is labeled Our Method. In both panels, image data flows upward. Each panel starts with a row of sample image grids (sketch, painting, real photo) with color-coded dashed boxes labeled Target T3, T2, T1 and Source S, drawn with triangle, square and circle glyphs. The images feed into a Feature Extractor bar. The extractor connects to a disentanglement encoder-decoder that splits features into F_s (domain-specific) and F_i (invariant). On the left, F_s is discarded into a trash can and three separate models, Model3, Model2 and Model1, are shown in a red box. On the right, the causal feature is highlighted by a red dashed box and feeds one unified Model. A small structural causal model graph with nodes D, F_s, F_i, X and Y sits in the top-right corner, with the Guide arrow in red.

abstract: Multi-target domain adaptation (MTDA) trains a model using a labeled source domain and several unlabeled target domains, aiming to enhance performance across all targets. However, existing methods lack a principled causal formulation and often rely on empirical domain-invariance enforcement, which can bias adaptation across targets. To fill this gap, we propose the **U**nbiased, **U**nconfounding, and **U**nified **C**ausal **F**ramework (**U$^3$CF**) for MTDA. To *unify* the alignment of multiple domains, we propose a prototype-driven alignment strategy that progressively updates prototypes by high-confidence target predictions, while the contrastive optimization objective jointly aligns target samples to semantic prototypes and preserves class discrimination. By formulating a structural causal model, we reveal that domain-invariant causal factors and domain-specific factors shape representations and labels, while the latter induce spurious label correlations across targets. Accordingly, U$^3$CF achieves *unbiased* prediction by disentangling representations into invariant causal components and domain-specific confounders and applying conditional intervention to *block confounding* effects while preserving invariant semantics. To ensure precise disentanglement, we leverage mutual information theory to derive a principled criterion for feature separation. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate that U$^3$CF consistently outperforms leading methods.
